topic:
When unlabeled treatment records rescue causal estimation: the sharp annotation frontier. Fix known 0<epsilon<1/2. Observe n>=1 independent labeled records (X,A,Y) distributed as P and m>=0 independent unlabeled records (X,A) distributed as its SAME marginal P_XA, independent of the labeled sample. X is in the known alphabet [d], d>=2; A and Y are binary. All cell probabilities p_x>=0 summing to one are allowed, including null cells; epsilon<=e_x=P(A=1|X=x)<=1-epsilon on occupied cells; mu_ax=P(Y=1|A=a,X=x) is unrestricted in [0,1]. Neither p nor e is known. No smoothness, sparsity, effect homogeneity, outcome surrogacy, or minimum cell mass is assumed. Consistency and conditional exchangeability identify tau(P)=sum_x p_x(mu_1x-mu_0x). The target population is shared by both samples, and missing outcomes are by independent random labeling, not selected enrollment. Determine, up to constants depending only on epsilon, the minimax MSE R_epsilon(n,m,d)=inf_T sup_P E_(P^n x P_XA^m)[(T-tau(P))^2] over all measurable estimators, uniformly for n>=1,m>=0,d>=2. Exhibit a numerical rate r_epsilon(n,m,d) with no unspecified optimization over unknown laws, prove a total computable estimator attaining it and a matching lower bound in the same observation experiment for every regime. Derive necessary and sufficient growth conditions for R->0 and R=O(1/n) along arbitrary n->infinity sequences m_n,d_n. The sharp tradeoff must include the m=0 frontier, the finite-m transition, and the limiting known-propensity benchmark. Leave the exact rate formula open; do not obtain it by substituting n+m for n in the supervised rate. The new theorem is the unequal-information approximation/variance and indistinguishability frontier: outcome-bearing moments have n observations, while treatment/mass information has n+m. Consumer: Cheng, Ananthakrishnan and Cai, Biometrics 2021, Robust and efficient semi-supervised estimation of average treatment effects with application to electronic health records data, Sections 2.1 and 4 (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7758040/). Their IBD comparative-effectiveness study observes treatment/covariates in all records but validates outcomes through random chart review. The frontier supplies a baseline-only discrete-adjustment benchmark for choosing additional chart labels versus acquiring treatment-covariate records when working nuisance models are not trusted. It does not claim efficiency with their post-treatment surrogates or validate that data set under an unrestricted discrete model. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The presolve derived an inverse-count baseline and a mixed Chebyshev approximation linear in outcome-bearing masses, allowing one labeled factor and many treatment-only factorial factors. A signed prior preserves the entire marginal distribution of cell masses and propensities while changing conditional outcome marks; auxiliary-only observations then agree exactly, and the joint likelihood discrepancy requires labeled observations. Symbolic polynomial identities, ten finite-atom priors and nine joint-likelihood checks passed. The suggested rate min{1,1/n+[d/((n+m)log(en))]^2} remains conjectural; the original problem stays answer-open. Known-propensity, m=0, d=2, null-cell and large-m boundaries were checked, without claiming the complete theorem.
UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove the Section 4 uniform hybrid-risk lemma, including false-light polynomial tails, branch-mean variance and mass-weighted summation without dimension or m/n leakage. The lower-prior normalization, fixed-sample transfers and every G1-G8 gap also require independent proof.
EARLY KILL TEST: At epsilon=1/4 check both sides of the pilot threshold and whether exponential count tails absorb outside-region polynomial growth uniformly. Recheck the joint-prior likelihood and normalization cost. If these fail, restart the answer derivation within the original model rather than asserting the proposed rate or substituting a weaker theorem.
STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/stat_semisupervised_discrete_ate_annotation_frontier.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the sharp finite-sample minimax MSE for unrestricted discrete ATE estimation from n labeled (X,A,Y) records and m independent same-population outcome-unlabeled (X,A) records, including every transition between m=0 and effectively known P_XA.

source_refs.claim: The supervised m=0 model has minimax MSE of order 1/n plus a large-alphabet term of order d^2/(n^2 log^2 n), while knowing P_X alone need not improve ATE estimation because the propensity remains unknown.
source_refs.author: Zhenghao Zeng, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, Yanjun Han, Edward H. Kennedy

source_refs.claim: Outcome-unlabeled EHR records can improve ATE efficiency, but the results are local semiparametric statements under working nuisance models rather than a uniform discrete minimax frontier.
source_refs.author: David Cheng, Ashwin N. Ananthakrishnan, Tianxi Cai

source_refs.claim: The paper studies independent labeled (Y,A,X) and unlabeled (A,X) samples under nuisance-model conditions, not worst-case finite-alphabet rates with null cells.
source_refs.author: Abhishek Chakrabortty, Guorong Dai, Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen

source_refs.excerpt: a polynomial approximation of \(\phi\) on the overlap-restricted four-cell cone
its control-zero construction and Poisson-to-fixed-sample transfer are mapped at theorem-and-appendix granularity

open_problems.why_unsolved: The literature leaves a precise gap between supervised large-alphabet minimax theory and regular semi-supervised efficiency theory. The banked supervised estimator lifts polynomials in all four (X,A,Y) cell probabilities using one outcome-bearing sample, whereas the annotation experiment permits higher factorial powers of P_XA to use n+m observations but permits outcome-mark factors to use only n. Thus the first upper-bound step that changes is the mixed-factorial lift and its branch-mean covariance analysis. The supervised converse also changes materially: any least-favorable mixture that perturbs P_XA becomes visible to the auxiliary sample, so a sharp lower prior must preserve the complete P_XA marginal while separating conditional outcome marks through labeled observations alone.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit numerical rate r_epsilon(n,m,d), a total computable mixed-factorial heavy/light estimator with risk at most C_epsilon r_epsilon, a matching c_epsilon r_epsilon lower bound in the joint experiment for every n,m,d, and necessary-and-sufficient conditions for consistency and O(1/n) risk.

writing_exemplar.why: Its chart-review motivation and labeled-versus-unlabeled formulation provide the closest application-facing narrative for an annotation frontier.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Gold-standard outcomes require costly chart review -> treatment and covariates exist on a much larger EHR cohort -> auxiliary records may improve ATE estimation -> quantify exactly when and how many such records rescue unrestricted discrete adjustment.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its large-alphabet ATE estimator and moment-matching fuzzy-hypothesis converse, replacing the single count budget by separate outcome-mark and P_XA budgets.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It solves the m=0 boundary in essentially the same unrestricted discrete causal model.

method_exemplars.technique: Split rare and regular cells, approximate the rare-region functional by a near-best polynomial, and estimate its monomials with factorial moments while proving coefficient-sensitive variance bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired estimator has the same rare-cell approximation bottleneck, but admissible monomials must remain linear in labeled outcome marks while using pooled P_XA factorial factors.

method_exemplars.technique: Use best-polynomial-approximation duality to construct moment-matched priors and a logarithmic effective-sample-size lower bound.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The same duality can yield the large-d converse once the priors are additionally constrained to agree exactly on the auxiliary marginal.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize the minimax value-of-information lattice for auxiliary samples observing X alone versus (X,A), and for oracle knowledge of P_X, e(X), or P_XA, in the same unrestricted finite-alphabet ATE model.

source_refs.claim: Knowing P_X need not accelerate unrestricted discrete ATE estimation because the relevant functional still depends on the unknown propensity.
source_refs.author: Zhenghao Zeng, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, Yanjun Han, Edward H. Kennedy

source_refs.claim: The paper analyzes auxiliary samples with and without observed treatment asymptotically, but does not compare these observation experiments by uniform minimax risk.
source_refs.author: Abhishek Chakrabortty, Guorong Dai, Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen

source_refs.claim: The paper derives regular semiparametric efficiency bounds for one- and two-sample ATE estimation with unlabeled covariates, rather than large-alphabet minimax equivalence or separation.
source_refs.author: Masahiro Kato

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing results isolate the obstruction but do not quantify it uniformly: P_X information alone leaves the propensity component unknown, while treatment-annotated auxiliaries constrain both p_x e_x and p_x(1-e_x). The first lower-bound step therefore differs across experiments: X-only auxiliaries require least-favorable pairs to agree on p_x, whereas (X,A) auxiliaries require agreement on both treatment-arm masses. Regular efficiency comparisons do not determine whether these experiments are rate-equivalent or strictly separated when d grows and occupied cells may have arbitrarily small mass.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A table of explicit minimax rates for the X-only, XA, known-P_X, known-e, and known-P_XA experiments, with rate-equivalence and strict-separation conditions for every pair as functions of n,m,d.

writing_exemplar.why: Its information-value discussion pinpoints the unknown propensity as the obstruction after P_X is revealed.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: High-dimensional adjustment creates unseen cells -> auxiliary distributional information appears valuable -> P_X alone leaves propensity uncertainty -> identify the minimal auxiliary annotation that changes the ATE rate.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct orthogonal semi-supervised ATE estimators separately when treatment is and is not observed in the auxiliary sample, and compare their score expansions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Those observation patterns are adjacent nodes of the proposed lattice and reveal which nuisance component each auxiliary variable can estimate.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive labeled- and unlabeled-stratum efficient influence functions and attain the resulting bound with generalized Riesz regression.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its two-stratum efficiency decomposition is the regular-model analogue of the desired minimax comparison.

method_exemplars.technique: Compare discrete causal-functional experiments by varying which nuisance distributions are treated as known and prove corresponding lower bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination asks for the same comparison with graded finite auxiliary samples and treatment annotation explicitly varied.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the semi-supervised minimax ATE frontier under a known shrinking bound sigma on cell-effect heterogeneity, resolving how unlabeled P_XA records alter the supervised residual wedge between occupancy-weighted and polynomial estimators.

source_refs.excerpt: The shrinking-radius frontier within the displayed residual wedge remains an acknowledged open question.
Add an adaptive-radius extension or a lower bound showing the price of adaptation to unknown sigma

open_problems.why_unsolved: Even in the supervised experiment, the banked upper and lower rates differ in a shrinking-radius wedge because the converse gives a product-scaled separation while the selector upper bound takes the minimum of polynomial and collision branches. Auxiliary P_XA observations alter these branches asymmetrically: occupancy weights and unmarked factorial factors can exploit n+m observations, while cell-effect marks still require n. The first proof step that changes is the signed one-mark covariance calculation; a matching lower channel must preserve P_XA exactly while enforcing the heterogeneity radius realization by realization.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A two-sided minimax characterization R(n,m,d,sigma) with explicit capped regimes and a computable selector, or a counterexample proving that the supervised residual wedge persists despite arbitrarily many auxiliary P_XA records.

writing_exemplar.why: Its annotation-economy framing can motivate effect dispersion as the structural condition determining the value of unlabeled records.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Outcome annotations are scarce -> treatment-covariate records reveal occupancy but not cell effects -> bounded effect dispersion may permit a sharper annotation frontier.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its approximate-homogeneity collision estimator and fuzzy lower subclasses while forcing identical P_XA mixtures in the auxiliary experiment.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The resolution must recover its supervised homogeneous and unrestricted-heterogeneity endpoints while determining the interior sigma dependence.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct a signed one-mark polynomial estimator whose unmarked factorial factors use pooled treatment-covariate counts, with a mixed-order variance proof.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This is the structurally analogous large-alphabet machinery needed for the polynomial branch of the sigma-indexed rate.

open_problems.open_problem: Develop honest confidence intervals for the discrete ATE whose coverage is uniform over all allowed laws and all n,m,d regimes and whose expected length is minimax-optimal across the semi-supervised annotation transition.

source_refs.claim: Bias-aware confidence intervals can remain valid when root-n inference fails, but their theory imposes smoothness or shape restrictions rather than unrestricted discrete rare-cell structure.
source_refs.author: Timothy B. Armstrong, Michal Kolesar

source_refs.claim: The two-sample ATE estimator is asymptotically normal and efficient under nuisance product-rate conditions and regular sample-size asymptotics.
source_refs.author: Masahiro Kato

source_refs.claim: Low-dimensional discrete plug-in estimators admit asymptotic-normal inference, while the large-d minimax analysis is stated in MSE and includes a nonparametric consistency threshold.
source_refs.author: Zhenghao Zeng, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, Yanjun Han, Edward H. Kennedy

source_refs.excerpt: The paper does not address deteriorating overlap, latent effect groups, inference

open_problems.why_unsolved: Regular semi-supervised influence-function theory requires nuisance rates and sampling regimes that fail when d approaches or exceeds the effective cell-count sample size, while a rate-optimal rare-cell polynomial estimator can have approximation bias comparable to its stochastic error and need not be Gaussian. Null and rare cells also make plug-in variance estimation nonuniform. The banked proposals establish squared-risk bounds but no limit law or honest coverage, and auxiliary records add two-sample conditional randomness. The missing proof must replace second-moment aggregation by uniform tail or distributional control for the mixed marked/unmarked polynomial and establish a confidence-length lower bound in the same experiment.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A computable confidence set C_n,m,d with uniform coverage at least 1-alpha-o(1), worst-case expected length matching a same-experiment minimax lower bound, and a characterization of the regimes admitting root-n Gaussian calibration versus bias-aware or non-Gaussian calibration.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the closest motivation arc for inference that explicitly acknowledges non-negligible worst-case bias.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Unconfoundedness identifies the ATE -> flexible adjustment introduces non-negligible bias -> conventional Wald intervals can undercover -> construct honest intervals at the actual information frontier.

method_exemplars.technique: Optimize weights against worst-case bias and variance, inflate critical values using the bias-to-standard-error ratio, and prove expected-length optimality.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired interval must likewise retain approximation bias explicitly, although its bias set comes from rare discrete cells and unequal sample information.

method_exemplars.technique: Use separate labeled- and unlabeled-stratum influence functions, cross-fitting, and a two-component variance estimator to establish asymptotic normality.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Any regular-regime branch must account for the two independent information sources before rare-cell bias corrections are added.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine finite-sample bias and variance control for discrete ATE estimators with the low-dimensional asymptotic-normal branch.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its supervised bias bounds and CLT identify the endpoints that a semi-supervised honest interval must interpolate.

open_problems.open_problem: Find the minimax-optimal cost-constrained outcome-validation design when labeling probabilities may depend on the observed (X,A) cell, without minimum cell masses, outcome models, or pilot-consistency assumptions.

source_refs.claim: Optimal two-phase sampling chooses outcome-measurement probabilities from auxiliary variables and costs to minimize semiparametric variance, relying on pilot information about conditional moments.
source_refs.author: Peter B. Gilbert, Xuesong Yu, Andrea Rotnitzky

source_refs.claim: The motivating EHR application obtains gold-standard outcomes through limited manual chart review, making the number and placement of outcome labels an operational choice.
source_refs.author: David Cheng, Ashwin N. Ananthakrishnan, Tianxi Cai

source_refs.claim: Unrestricted high-dimensional discrete confounding creates a rare-cell minimax barrier outside ordinary semiparametric design calculations.
source_refs.author: Zhenghao Zeng, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, Yanjun Han, Edward H. Kennedy

open_problems.why_unsolved: Classical two-phase design minimizes an oracle efficient-influence-function variance using estimated conditional outcome variances. In the unrestricted discrete model, rare and unseen cells create approximation bias that cannot be captured by that regular objective, and the conditional moments needed for pilot allocation need not be uniformly estimable. The first proof step that changes is therefore the design criterion itself: assignment-dependent variance must be optimized jointly with worst-case rare-cell approximation bias, followed by a lower bound over all adaptive validation policies.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A characterization of the optimal cellwise labeling rule under a total expected labeling-cost constraint, a computable pilot-free or sequential design-estimator pair attaining an explicit minimax MSE, and a matching lower bound over all admissible adaptive validation policies.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames expensive outcome measurement as a joint design-and-estimation problem and makes the cost-precision tradeoff explicit.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Auxiliaries are cheap and broadly observed -> definitive outcomes are expensive -> simple random validation can waste information -> choose validation probabilities and an estimator jointly under worst-case rare-cell risk.

method_exemplars.technique: Minimize efficient-influence-function variance under a measurement-cost constraint, then pair the design with augmented inverse-probability estimation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This is the donor allocation argument, but the destination objective must add minimax rare-cell approximation error and cannot assume stable pilot nuisance estimation.

method_exemplars.technique: Control worst-case discrete ATE bias and variance cell by cell and certify necessity using moment-matched lower priors.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Those bounds supply the nonregular component missing from classical two-phase design and can be made allocation-dependent through cellwise labeled counts.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine outcome imputation with inverse-propensity residual correction to use auxiliary records while retaining robustness to outcome-model misspecification.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest ATE estimation architecture for chart-review labels and supplies the regular branch to combine with a minimax validation design.

literature_map:
1. Hahn (1998, Econometrica) supplies the regular semiparametric efficiency benchmark for ATE under ignorability, but not a growing-alphabet minimax analysis.
2. Hirano, Imbens and Ridder (2003, Econometrica) show regular-model efficiency gains from estimated propensities; rare discrete cells make that comparison nonuniform.
3. Cheng, Ananthakrishnan and Cai (2021, Biometrics; arXiv:1804.00195) motivate outcome annotation through EHR chart review and prove robust, locally efficient semi-supervised ATE estimation.
4. Chakrabortty, Dai and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2022, arXiv:2201.00468) study independent labeled (Y,A,X) and unlabeled (A,X) samples, plus a treatment-unobserved variant, under nuisance-model conditions.
5. Hou, Mukherjee and Cai (2025, JMLR; arXiv:2110.12336) derive efficient and doubly robust ATE estimators when treatment and outcome are partially annotated and noisy surrogates are available.
6. Xu, Witten and Shojaie (2025, arXiv:2502.17741) give a general regular semiparametric framework for safe and efficient semi-supervised inference.
7. Kato (2025, arXiv:2511.08303) derives one- and two-sample efficient influence functions and fixed-ratio asymptotic normality via generalized Riesz regression.
8. Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han and Kennedy (2024, arXiv:2405.00118) establish the supervised large-alphabet discrete-ATE rate and consistency threshold.
9. Zeng et al. also show that knowing P_X alone need not improve unrestricted discrete ATE estimation because the unknown propensity remains in the relevant functional.
10. Jiao, Venkat, Han and Weissman (2015, IEEE TIT; arXiv:1406.6956) develop localized best-polynomial estimators and factorial-moment analysis for nonsmooth large-alphabet functionals.
11. Wu and Yang (2016, IEEE TIT; arXiv:1407.0381) establish approximation-duality lower bounds and logarithmic effective-sample-size enlargement; their later unseen-mass work refines fixed-sample transfers.
12. Armstrong and Kolesar (2021, Econometrica; arXiv:1712.04594) construct bias-aware honest ATE intervals under smoothness or shape restrictions, showing that an MSE rate alone does not settle inference.
13. Gilbert, Yu and Rotnitzky (2014, Statistics in Medicine; doi:10.1002/sim.6006) optimize two-phase outcome validation using auxiliary-dependent costs and conditional variances under regular pilot conditions.
14. Levis et al. (2024, Statistics in Medicine; arXiv:2204.02432) study identification and efficient ATE estimation with informatively missing EHR outcomes, but not large-alphabet minimax risk.
15. The central unresolved tension is that semi-supervised work quantifies regular asymptotic efficiency while discrete-functional work quantifies rare-cell minimax difficulty; no located paper joins them in the unequal n-versus-(n+m) experiment.
